_readme: Surface templates for the Hindi reasoning corpus. This file is intended to be edited
by hand: it is the place where human-authored templates live alongside the
generated ones. Run `python -m common.reasoning.check_templates --language hindi`
after editing: it validates the schema, checks every literal word against the Hindi
pretraining corpus, and prints a rendered example of each template.
Each template has two parts. `fact` is emitted once per entity (value_compare) or
once per adjacent pair (chain); `question` is emitted once at the end. Splitting
them this way is what lets one template cover 2, 3 or 4 entities, which is how the
held-out longer-chain test split is built without writing separate templates for it.
Placeholders need not be written by hand. A sentence written with real
words and convert it:  python -m common.reasoning.make_template --language hindi
--fact "<one statement>" --question "<the question>" --type argmax
prints a finished template to paste here, and names any word it did not
recognise. The placeholder list below is reference, not a prerequisite.
PLACEHOLDERS
{e0} {e1} {e2} ...  entity name by position
{ea} {eb}           the two entities of one chain link (inside `fact` only)
{e}  {v}            entity and its value (inside a value_compare `fact` only)
{efirst} {elast}    first and last entity of a chain (inside `question` only)
{attr} {poss}       attribute noun and its possessive  (उम्र, की)
{noun_gender}       not a placeholder - selects {who_poss} automatically
{unit} {cop}        unit and copula                    (साल, है)
{than}              comparison particle                (से)
{more} {less}       invariant quantifiers              (ज्यादा, कम)
{sup_more} {sup_less}  superlatives                    (सबसे ज्यादा, सबसे कम)
{who} {who_poss}    interrogatives                     (कौन, किसकी/किसका)
{or} {equal}        disjunction and equality           (या, बराबर)
{fs} {qm}           full stop and question mark        (।, ?)
fact_reverse        chain only - the same link stated from the opposite end, so the larger entity is not always named first
FIELDS
id             unique, stable - referenced in the results tables
family         value_compare | chain
question_type  argmax | argmin | relation
split          train | heldout   (heldout templates build test_template)
author         generated | user  (provenance, reported honestly in the writeup)
A NOTE ON WHAT MAKES A GOOD TEMPLATE: vary the word order and register, not the
vocabulary. The vocabulary is already corpus-validated; new words would have to go
through candidates.py instead. Templates that only swap synonyms add little, while
templates that reorder the clause genuinely test whether the model learned the
relation or a fixed word sequence.

templates.question: {attr} {sup_more} {who_poss} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: generated
templates.notes: word order variant: attribute fronted before the superlative

templates.question: {attr} में सबसे बड़ा {who} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 1, unchanged. First template to use `कौन` rather than किसकी/किसका, and the only one in the adjective register (सबसे बड़ा, 899).

templates.question: {entities} में से {who_poss} {attr} {more} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 2. Names its candidates explicitly — the shape that motivated the {entities} placeholder, since entity names previously could not appear in a question. `में से` 7,045.

templates.question: {less} {attr} {who_poss} {cop} इनमें से{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 3, with one correction: the original said `दोनों में से` ("of the two"), which would be false on the three-entity problems the brief also asks for. `इनमें से` (800) is count-neutral; the spaced spelling `इन में से` scores only 10.

templates.question: {who} {more} {attr} का {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 4, with `का` kept as literal text rather than the {poss} placeholder. Here the possessive agrees with कौन, not with the attribute noun, so substituting it by attribute gender produced the ungrammatical `कौन ज्यादा उम्र की है?`.

templates.question: इनमें से {who_poss} {attr} {less} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 5, unchanged. First template to open with the among-phrase.

templates.question: इनमें से {who_poss} {attr} {sup_more} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 6, with `इन सब में से` (4 occurrences) replaced by `इनमें से` (800). Puts the superlative at the end, which no other template does.

templates.question: {attr} में {sup_less} इनमें से {who} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 7, same `इन सब में से` substitution. Attribute fronted, among-phrase medial, `कौन` final — the most scrambled order in the set, hence held out.

templates.question: {sup_more} {who} {cop} {attr} में{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: user sample 8, with `इन दोनों में` dropped rather than substituted: `दोनों` is false on three-entity problems, and the sentence reads naturally without it. Keeps the original's distinctive superlative-first, attribute-last order.
